questions.scenario: You are teaching your friends how to play a very complex new board game. What is your approach?

options.text: I explain the big picture first, then break the rules down into clear, logical steps.
I send them a cool, fast-paced YouTube animation that explains the rules visually.
I let them play a 'practice round' so I can spot their mistakes and correct them immediately.
I change or simplify some of the harder rules so my younger sibling can play with us too.

questions.scenario: Your teacher assigns a massive group project. What role do you naturally take?

options.text: I create the outline, divide the topics, and plan the timeline for the whole group.
I volunteer to make the PowerPoint, adding cool transitions, graphics, and videos.
I keep checking the teacher's grading rubric to make sure we don't lose any points.
I make sure the shy kid in the group gets a task they feel comfortable doing.

questions.scenario: You are trying to learn a new skill (like coding or guitar) online. What kind of course do you love?

options.text: A structured 10-part series that takes me from beginner to expert in a clear order.
An interactive app where learning feels like playing a video game.
A course that gives me mini-quizzes at the end of each video to test my memory.
A video that has subtitles, clear transcripts, and offers multiple ways to understand the topic.

questions.scenario: You notice your friend is really struggling to understand Math. How do you help?

options.text: I rewrite their notes into a better, more organized summary.
I find a cool 3D simulator or interactive website that visually explains the formula.
I give them 5 practice problems to figure out exactly which step they are messing up.
I realize they have a short attention span, so I invent a completely different, fun way to study.

questions.scenario: You are designing a brand new school app for students. What is your favorite feature?

options.text: A master calendar that organizes all subjects, homework, and exams perfectly.
Sleek UI, dark mode, and gamified badges that you earn for completing tasks.
A detailed 'stats' page showing exactly how much your grades have improved over time.
Text-to-speech tools and dyslexic-friendly fonts so every student can use it easily.

questions.scenario: If you could change one thing about how your school works, what would it be?

options.text: Change the syllabus to include real-world skills like taxes and mental health.
Replace boring textbooks with iPads, VR headsets, and interactive digital labs.
Stop giving long, stressful final exams and replace them with better weekly check-ins.
Let students choose how they learn based on whether they are visual, auditory, or hands-on learners.

questions.scenario: You are playing a strategy or puzzle video game. What is the best part?

options.text: The feeling of unlocking new levels in a sequence that slowly gets harder.
The amazing graphics, sound design, and smooth controls.
Looking at my post-game stats to see my accuracy and where I need to improve.
The 'difficulty settings' that let anyone enjoy the game, from beginners to pros.

questions.scenario: You are organizing a weekend trip with your friends. What is your priority?

options.text: Making a solid itinerary so we know exactly what we are doing from morning to night.
Creating a shared digital map with cool pins and photos of places to visit.
Tracking the budget constantly so we don't run out of money by day two.
Making sure the restaurants we pick have options for our friend with food allergies.

questions.scenario: When you read a really good non-fiction book or article, what do you appreciate most?

options.text: How well the chapters are organized so the information flows perfectly.
The colorful diagrams, infographics, and pictures that break up the text.
The bullet points or summaries at the end of the chapter that highlight the facts.
How the author uses simple language to explain something incredibly difficult.

questions.scenario: You have to give a presentation to the class. What makes you feel confident?

options.text: Knowing my speech has a strong introduction, main body, and conclusion.
Knowing my slides look incredibly professional and visually stunning.
Knowing I have predicted the questions the teacher will ask and have answers ready.
Knowing I am speaking at a good pace so everyone in the room can follow along.

Curriculum_Developer.title: Curriculum Developer / Syllabus Designer
Curriculum_Developer.primary_match_text: You are a 'big picture' thinker who loves structure. You have a natural talent for breaking down massive amounts of information into logical, step-by-step journeys.
Curriculum_Developer.day_in_the_life: Designing the actual textbooks, syllabus, and learning roadmaps used by schools, universities, or corporate training programs.
Curriculum_Developer.alternative_match_text: Because you love organizing information and mapping out plans, designing educational curriculums is a great way to use your structural brain.
Curriculum_Developer.roadmap: Take Humanities or Science in 11th/12th. Pursue a BA/BSc in Education, Psychology, or your favorite subject, followed by a Master's in Curriculum and Instruction.

ELearning_Designer.title: E-Learning Designer / Instructional Technologist
ELearning_Designer.primary_match_text: You are a creative, tech-savvy visual thinker. You believe learning shouldn't be boring, and you love using digital tools to make things interactive and fun.
ELearning_Designer.day_in_the_life: Building interactive online courses, educational games, VR simulations, and educational videos for tech companies and universities.
ELearning_Designer.alternative_match_text: Since you love using technology to make content engaging and visual, designing interactive e-learning experiences is an incredible career match.
ELearning_Designer.roadmap: Any stream works in 11th/12th (Computer Science is a bonus). Pursue a degree in Educational Technology, Multimedia Design, or Computer Science.

Assessment_Specialist.title: Educational Assessment & Evaluation Specialist
Assessment_Specialist.primary_match_text: You are analytical and detail-oriented. You like knowing exactly how to measure success, spot mistakes, and figure out how to improve performance based on data.
Assessment_Specialist.day_in_the_life: Designing standardized tests, creating grading rubrics, and analyzing test data to figure out if students are actually learning what they are supposed to.
Assessment_Specialist.alternative_match_text: If you are great at analyzing performance and finding gaps, creating fair and accurate assessments for large educational boards is a unique and high-demand role.
Assessment_Specialist.roadmap: Take Science or Commerce (with Math/Stats) in 11th/12th. Pursue a degree in Statistics, Psychology, or Education, focusing on Educational Measurement.

Inclusive_Learning_Designer.title: Inclusive Learning / Accessibility Designer
Inclusive_Learning_Designer.primary_match_text: You are highly empathetic and a great problem solver. You naturally notice when systems leave people out, and you love adapting things so everyone gets a fair chance.
Inclusive_Learning_Designer.day_in_the_life: Modifying curriculums for students with ADHD, dyslexia, or physical disabilities, ensuring educational software is accessible (like screen-reader friendly).
Inclusive_Learning_Designer.alternative_match_text: Because you care deeply about fairness and empathy, a career ensuring that education is accessible to every type of brain and body is a highly fulfilling path.
Inclusive_Learning_Designer.roadmap: Take Humanities or Science in 11th/12th. Pursue a degree in Special Education, Psychology, or Human-Computer Interaction (HCI).
